item.title: Holy Cross captain ready to face former school in Deans elimination
item.description: The 17-year-old from Lavena, Taveuni will lead Holy Cross against Nasinu Secondary School, where he played in the Under-17 competition last season. Vodotagitagi says taking on his former teammates will be one of the toughest moments of his rugby journey because of the close friendships they built during their time together.
item.content:encoded:
The 17-year-old from Lavena, Taveuni will lead Holy Cross against Nasinu Secondary School, where he played in the Under-17 competition last season.

Vodotagitagi says taking on his former teammates will be one of the toughest moments of his rugby journey because of the close friendships they built during their time together.

While he expects the occasion to be emotional, he says his focus is leading Holy Cross and helping the team secure a place in the semi-finals.

The Holy Cross captain says the team's journey to the eliminations has not been easy.

He says they have trained with limited equipment, while some players have had to overcome challenges at home. He also says five players missed last week's match in Labasa after being suspended from school.

Despite those setbacks, Vodotagitagi says the team continued to encourage one another and remained determined to keep winning.

He says many of the players are from the Northern Division and tomorrow's match will be their first opportunity to play on the big stage in Suva.

Vodotagitagi says while some of the boys are nervous, most are excited and ready for the challenge.

He says facing familiar faces will make tomorrow's match special, but once the whistle blows, his full attention will be on leading Holy Cross in their bid for a place in the Vodafone Deans Trophy Under-18 semi-finals.

Holy Cross College will take on Nasinu Secondary School at 12.20pm while Suva Grammar will face Ratu Luke Secondary School at 1.50pm.

Both games will be held at the Grammar Ground.

At St Vincent Ground, Lelean Memorial School will face Marist Brothers High School at 12.20pm, while Ratu Kadavulevu School will take on Ratu Sukuna Memorial School at 1.50pm.

Meanwhile, Queen Victoria School will travel to Lawaqa Park to face Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute at 10am, while Cuvu College will take on St John's College at 1pm.

At Ratu Ganilau Park, Ratu Navula College will face Shiri Guru Nanak Khalsa College at 2pm, before Ra High School meets Navatu Secondary School at 3.25pm.

item.title: Ra defeats Northland 17-10 in Vanua Championship final while Yasawa beats Nadroga in the Ranadi final
item.description: Ra claimed a hard-fought 17-10 victory over Northland in front of a sell-out crowd in the Vodafone Vanua Championship final at Buckhurst Park in Suva this afternoon. The clash attracted a massive turnout, with fans from both teams still queuing up outside the venue at half time after tickets were sold out.
item.content:encoded:
Ra claimed a hard-fought 17-10 victory over Northland in front of a sell-out crowd in the Vodafone Vanua Championship final at Buckhurst Park in Suva this afternoon.

The clash attracted a massive turnout, with fans from both teams still queuing up outside the venue at half time after tickets were sold out.

The overwhelming demand prompted officials to print additional tickets to accommodate spectators.

Ra halfback, Peni Matawalu delivered an outstanding performance, controlling the tempo of the match and guiding Ra to a memorable victory.

The atmosphere was electric throughout the contest, with supporters cheering passionately as both teams gave everything for their vanua in a fiercely contested encounter.

Buckhurst Park was awash in red, with Ra supporters significantly outnumbering Northland fans and providing a vocal home-ground advantage that inspired their team to a historic win.

Ra now qualifies for the 2027 Skipper Cup Competition.

In other results, Yasawa defeated Nadroga 43-15 in Royal Tea Ranadi final while Macuata thumped Cakaudrove 30-10 in the Under-20 final.

item.title: Fiji Pearls receive $150,840 boost ahead of World Cup qualifiers
item.description: The Fiji Sports Commission has provided a $150,840 grant to the Fiji Netball Association to support the Fiji Pearls' preparations for the upcoming Netball World Cup Qualifiers in Tonga. The cheque was presented by Fiji Sports Commission Chairman Peter Mazey to Fiji Pearls head coach Michelle Parsons and Fiji Netball Association board member Vasiti Vocea.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Sports Commission has provided a $150,840 grant to the Fiji Netball Association to support the Fiji Pearls' preparations for the upcoming Netball World Cup Qualifiers in Tonga.

The cheque was presented by Fiji Sports Commission Chairman Peter Mazey to Fiji Pearls head coach Michelle Parsons and Fiji Netball Association board member Vasiti Vocea.

Mazey says the funding reflects the Commission's commitment to helping the national side prepare effectively for the tournament, expressing confidence that the financial support will strengthen the team's campaign.

The grant will help cover key preparation costs as the Fiji Pearls gear up to compete for qualification to the Netball World Cup.

Fiji Netball Head Coach Michelle Parsons thanked the Commission for the sponsorship as preparations for Tonga intensify .

Parsons says she aims to get Fiji Netball back into the top 10.

She says they are currently ranked 18th and she wants to bring Fiji Netball back to its glory days.

Fiji will compete in the World Qualifiers in Tonga from September 14th to the 19th.

item.title: Experienced Matawalu eyes Vanua Championship glory
item.description: Former FIJI Water Flying Fijians and Swire Shipping Fijian Drua half-back Peni Matawalu will once again be at the heart of his side's campaign when they take on Northland in the Vanua Championship final this afternoon. Matawalu has been instrumental in his team's run to the decider, producing commanding performances in both the quarter-final and semi-final to help steer his side into the final.
item.content:encoded:
Former FIJI Water Flying Fijians and Swire Shipping Fijian Drua half-back Peni Matawalu will once again be at the heart of his side's campaign when they take on Northland in the Vanua Championship final this afternoon.

Matawalu has been instrumental in his team's run to the decider, producing commanding performances in both the quarter-final and semi-final to help steer his side into the final.

His quick service, sharp decision-making, and speed around the fringes make him one of the key players to watch.

The Ra scrum-half controlled the tempo of last week's semi-final against a determined Cakaudrove outfit, using his experience, composure, and game management to guide his team to victory.

The younger brother of former Flying Fijians half-back and winger Nikola Matawalu, Peni is expected to play another pivotal role in today's final.

Ra has booked a place in the Skipper Cup for next season in 2027, and they will play Northland in the final at 3pm today at the Buckhurst Park in Suva.

In the under 20 Vanua Championships, Macuata faces Cakaudrove at 11am and in the Royal Tea Ranadi final Yasawa faces Nadroga at 1pm in Suva.

item.title: Southern Zone ready to take on the east - Wadali
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 30/07/2026 President of the Vodafone Deans Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Association, Rusiate Wadali, says Southern Zone teams are well prepared to take on their Eastern Zone counterparts in this weekend's Under-18 elimination round.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 30/07/2026

President of the Vodafone Deans Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Association, Rusiate Wadali, says Southern Zone teams are well prepared to take on their Eastern Zone counterparts in this weekend's Under-18 elimination round.

Marist Brothers High School and Ratu Sukuna Memorial School will travel to St Vincent Ground, where they will face Lelean Memorial School and Ratu Kadavulevu School respectively.

Wadali says although the matches will be played in the East, coaches have been urged to step up their preparations to ensure the players are ready.

He says the Southern Zone has the highest number of teams that qualified for the national eliminations and they are ready to take on the challenge.

Insert: Wadali on South ready – 30 July 2026

The Under-18 elimination matches will be played at four venues this Saturday: St Vincent Ground in Tailevu, Grammar Ground in Suva, Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka and Ratu Ganilau Park in Savusavu.

At St Vincent Ground, Lelean Memorial School will face Marist Brothers High School at 12.20pm, while Ratu Kadavulevu School will take on Ratu Sukuna Memorial School at 1.50pm.

At Grammar Ground, Nasinu Secondary School will play Holy Cross College at 12.20pm, while Suva Grammar School will meet Ratu Luke Secondary School.

Meanwhile, Queen Victoria School will travel to Lawaqa Park to face Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute at 10am, while Cuvu College will take on St John's College at 1pm.

At Ratu Ganilau Park, Ratu Navula College will face Shiri Guru Nanak Khalsa College at 2pm, before Ra High School meets Navatu Secondary School at 3.25pm.

item.title: Ba and Labasa set for title-defining Extra Premier League showdown
item.description: Football fans are in for one of the biggest matches of the 2026 Extra Premier League season tomorrow as league leaders Dayal's Sawmillers Ba FC travel to Subrail Park to take on Extra Supermarket Labasa FC, with just one point separating the two sides in the title race. Separated by just one point, the two teams are locked in a tight title race, with Ba leading the standings on 33 points and Labas
item.content:encoded:
Football fans are in for one of the biggest matches of the 2026 Extra Premier League season tomorrow as league leaders Dayal's Sawmillers Ba FC travel to Subrail Park to take on Extra Supermarket Labasa FC, with just one point separating the two sides in the title race.

Separated by just one point, the two teams are locked in a tight title race, with Ba leading the standings on 33 points and Labasa close behind on 32.

Defending champions Rewa FC remain in contention on 29 points, making tomorrow's result crucial in the battle for the championship.

A win for Ba would see the Men in Black open up a four-point lead with only two matches remaining, leaving them one victory away from securing a record-extending 22nd league title.

However, a victory for Labasa would see the Babasiga Lions move to the top of the standings and take control of the title race heading into the final two rounds.

The match brings together the competition's two most consistent teams this season.

The clash also carries extra significance for Ba, which is chasing its first league title since the 2018-19 season.

For Labasa, dropping points at home could prove costly.

item.title: OFC to review FIFA's private investment proposal next month
item.description: The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) says FIFA has started a consultation process with its Member Associations and the FIFA Council on the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise initiative. OFC says the proposal will be considered by its Executive Committee at its upcoming meeting in August.
item.content:encoded:
The Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) says FIFA has started a consultation process with its Member Associations and the FIFA Council on the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise initiative.

OFC says the proposal will be considered by its Executive Committee at its upcoming meeting in August.

The Confederation has invited its Member Associations to review the proposal and participate in the consultation process.

OFC says it remains committed to constructive engagement with its Member Associations, FIFA, other Confederations and football stakeholders throughout the consultation process, while supporting the continued development of football across Oceania and globally.

Meanwhile, UEFA and its 55 member associations have voted to boycott all FIFA competitions if FIFA member associations approve plans to sell stakes in its competitions to private investors.

FIFA announced plans to create a new commercial company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would manage competitions including the FIFA World Cup; private investors would be allowed to buy minority shares in the new company.

UEFA strongly opposed the proposal, saying the FIFA World Cup is "not for sale" and should never be treated as an investment product.

If approved by FIFA's 211 member associations, UEFA said it would boycott all FIFA tournaments, including the men's and women's World Cups and the Club World Cup.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has urged member associations to support the proposal, offering up to US$40 million in funding for those who vote in favour and associations have until September 19th to accept the plan.
